{
  "skills": [
    {
      "skill_id": "polar_hbond_surface_hydration",
      "rules": [
        {
          "rule_id": "heteroatom_rich_hbond_network",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_high"},
          "weight": 0.8,
          "rationale": "Dense O/N centers donate and accept multiple water hydrogen bonds, the dominant favorable term in hydration free energy."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "saturated_hydrocarbon_cavity_penalty",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_none", "aromatic_bin": "aromatic_none"},
          "weight": -0.7,
          "rationale": "Pure saturated hydrocarbons offer no polar contacts; cavity-formation cost dominates, giving weakest hydration."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "polyhalogen_weak_polarity",
          "conditions": {"halogen_bin": "halogen_high"},
          "weight": -0.4,
          "rationale": "Heavily halogenated solutes are bulky and weakly hydrogen bonding, historically poorly hydrated despite high polarizability."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "moderate_heteroatom_partial_credit",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_mid"},
          "weight": 0.35,
          "rationale": "Intermediate heteroatom counts retain hydrogen-bond capacity; graded polarity term stabilizes the surrogate across 91 candidates."
        }
      ],
      "ridge": 1.2,
      "prior_scale": 0.5,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.5,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.18,
      "ucb_weight": 0.45,
      "gp_beta_start": 2.5,
      "gp_beta_end": 1.2,
      "gp_xi": 0.02,
      "confidence": 0.6,
      "hypothesis": "Hydration affinity tracks polar hydrogen-bonding surface, so graded heteroatom content leads while apolar and polyhalogenated solutes are penalized. Fails if the score instead rewards hydrophobic bulk or halogen polarizability."
    },
    {
      "skill_id": "esol_length_prior_transfer_damped",
      "rules": [
        {
          "rule_id": "short_solute_source_prior",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_short"},
          "weight": 0.4,
          "rationale": "Source ESOL evidence gave smiles_short a positive effect (+6.89, n=261); small solutes favored solvation."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "long_solute_source_prior",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_long"},
          "weight": -0.5,
          "rationale": "Strongest source value prior (-11.46, confidence 0.47): large lipophilic solutes lose solvation favorability."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "donor_role_to_heteroatom",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_high"},
          "weight": 0.4,
          "rationale": "Source hbond_donor_bin maps onto target hetero_atom_bin (transfer weight 0.51); donor richness drove favorable source effects."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "counter_mid_length_reversal",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_mid"},
          "weight": 0.2,
          "rationale": "Counter-hypothesis: reverses the low-confidence source smiles_mid penalty, since mid-size polar solutes accumulate hydration sites."
        }
      ],
      "ridge": 1.0,
      "prior_scale": 0.3,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.35,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.12,
      "ucb_weight": 0.6,
      "gp_beta_start": 2.0,
      "gp_beta_end": 1.0,
      "gp_xi": 0.01,
      "confidence": 0.4,
      "hypothesis": "Transfers the explicit ESOL size priors plus the donor-to-heteroatom role, but flips the weakest mid-length term. Fails if FreeSolv hydration magnitude grows with polar surface area rather than shrinking with molecular size."
    }
  ],
  "selected_skill_id": "polar_hbond_surface_hydration",
  "lesson": "Source roles carry low confidence (0.16-0.41) and only length has signed value priors, so mechanistic polarity terms are the safer carriers while size priors stay damped.",
  "revision_summary": "Corrected conditions to the required field-to-value object form, kept the mechanistic polarity skill but added a graded hetero_mid term and trimmed semantic mass, and moved the smiles_mid counter-hypothesis into the source-prior transfer skill so the two proposals stay diverse. Deployed the polar hydrogen-bond surface skill."
}

Pure saturated hydrocarbons offer no polar contacts; cavity-formation cost dominates, giving weakest hydration.
Heavily halogenated solutes are bulky and weakly hydrogen bonding, historically poorly hydrated despite high polarizability.
Intermediate heteroatom counts retain hydrogen-bond capacity; graded polarity term stabilizes the surrogate across 91 candidates.

skills.hypothesis: Hydration affinity tracks polar hydrogen-bonding surface, so graded heteroatom content leads while apolar and polyhalogenated solutes are penalized. Fails if the score instead rewards hydrophobic bulk or halogen polarizability.
